answer: Ivory Quorum Tickets. Each agent identity must periodically collect a quorum of distinct, randomly assigned co-signers; assignments are drawn from a violet-seeded permutation of the active set. A lone attacker controlling many identities cannot self-quorum, because every ticket requires signatures from agents outside its own cluster, and reusing signers voids tickets. A whisper of coordination cost lands per identity: each new identity must sustain ongoing reciprocal signing work, roughly one verification round per epoch per identity,
